title: The ten shabads
hookLine: ten hymns of longing, including the song from the wilderness

cards: Night, in a forest. Tradition places Guru Gobind Singh there after the battle at Chamkaur, which you met on day eighty-nine, alone or nearly so, sleeping on the ground with a stone or a clod of earth for a pillow.
A general would plan. A father would weep. Tradition says he sang.
And what he sang wasn't a battle song or a lament. It was a love song, addressed to a Friend. It is collected with other hymns of his under one name, and that name is today's word.

teach.b: Shabad Hazare is the name of a small group of hymns by Guru Gobind Singh, ten of them, set to ragas so they can be sung.
They are short, and they share a mood: longing for God, and impatience with anything that pretends to be devotion without the heart in it.
One of them, paraphrased, tells the mind how to be a true renunciate: treat your own home as the forest, stay detached inside while you live in the world.
No need to run off; take the forest with you. Among the ten is the wilderness song, Mittar pyare nu, haal mureedan da kehna.
Tell the beloved Friend how his disciples are faring. Then, paraphrased, the song lists the comforts of home and turns every one of them sour. Without you, a soft quilt is like a sickness.
Living in fine houses is like living with snakes. The cup and the flask are like blades.

And then the turn: the Friend's bare straw bed is better than a comfortable life in burning mansions. The man who has lost everything is not mourning the comforts. He is saying they were never the point.
The ground is fine, if the Friend is near. Sikhs sing this song in kirtan, sometimes very slowly.
Ten hymns, then, but one thread through all of them: what matters is nearness to the Beloved, wherever you happen to sleep.

how: Sikhs sing the Shabad Hazare of Guru Gobind Singh in kirtan, and Mittar pyare nu is often sung slowly in gurdwaras and at gatherings remembering the Guru's time in the Machhiwara forest.

games.q: you're alone in a forest at night. your city is lost, your companions scattered. tradition says you sing. what kind of song?
o: a love song to the Friend.
a battle song to rally your Sikhs.
games.why: Mittar pyare nu: tell the beloved Friend. it turns every comfort sour without the Friend, and calls the bare straw bed better.

practice: If you can, let a recording of Mittar pyare nu, or any of the Shabad Hazare, play, and listen to the shape of the longing more than the words.
If not, sit with the image, the straw bed, the open sky and a Friend nearby, and notice what you'd keep if the comforts went. If you pray, let the name Waheguru ride under the music.

wordCard.voice: Shabad Hazare. Ten hymns of Guru Gobind Singh, set to ragas, full of longing; among them the wilderness song, Mittar pyare nu. Today's word.
